The field briefing

One page for the walk. Each figure carries a mark that says whether it was measured, derived, assumed or simulated.

FIELD BRIEFINGDirect route, S0 to S1
measured derived assumed simulated

Objective

  • Sample one hollow and one adjacent ridge of the boxwork unit, to learn why the ridges resisted erosion.

Route

  • Start at S0, a notional rover park at the edge of the unit
  • Distance 540 m, climb 40 m
  • Shortest in time. 31% of it crosses ground steeper than 10°.
  • Out 17 min, back 14 min, at the station 30 min
  • Whole walk about 1 h 01 min

Hazards

  • Steepest ground on the route 20°
  • Ground over 20° is treated as blocked

Conditions

  • Air -71 to -5 °C, ground -84 to 4 °C
  • Daylight 06:46 to 18:51 local time, sky sunny

Radiation

  • 0.67 mSv per Mars day at Gale crater (Curiosity RAD, 2012 to 2013)
  • About 0.03 mSv for this walk. The same on either route.

What the rover found

  • Curiosity drilled this hollow in October 2025 and the ridge top beside it, Nevado Sajama, in November 2025.

Limits

  • Rocks smaller than about 1 m are not in the terrain model.
  • Walking speed is an Earth hiking model scaled by an assumed suit factor of 0.5.
  • The slope limit is our assumption, not a NASA limit.
  • Sand, dust and wind are not modelled.
  • Conditions are from sol 4995 (2026-08-25), not today.
  • The radiation rate is quoted from a summary of the 2014 paper. The team has not yet read the paper itself.
FIELD BRIEFINGCautious route, S0 to S1
measured derived assumed simulated

Objective

  • Sample one hollow and one adjacent ridge of the boxwork unit, to learn why the ridges resisted erosion.

Route

  • Start at S0, a notional rover park at the edge of the unit
  • Distance 630 m, climb 41 m
  • About 90 m longer than Direct. Only 5% of it crosses ground steeper than 10°.
  • Out 19 min, back 15 min, at the station 30 min
  • Whole walk about 1 h 04 min

Hazards

  • Steepest ground on the route 20°
  • Ground over 20° is treated as blocked

Conditions

  • Air -71 to -5 °C, ground -84 to 4 °C
  • Daylight 06:46 to 18:51 local time, sky sunny

Radiation

  • 0.67 mSv per Mars day at Gale crater (Curiosity RAD, 2012 to 2013)
  • About 0.03 mSv for this walk. The same on either route.

What the rover found

  • Curiosity drilled this hollow in October 2025 and the ridge top beside it, Nevado Sajama, in November 2025.

Limits

  • Rocks smaller than about 1 m are not in the terrain model.
  • Walking speed is an Earth hiking model scaled by an assumed suit factor of 0.5.
  • The slope limit is our assumption, not a NASA limit.
  • Sand, dust and wind are not modelled.
  • Conditions are from sol 4995 (2026-08-25), not today.
  • The radiation rate is quoted from a summary of the 2014 paper. The team has not yet read the paper itself.

Sources and status

Data

  • NASA Mars Trek, HiRISE mosaic tiles
  • USGS, Mars MSL Gale Merged DEM 1m
  • NASA, Curiosity waypoints
  • NASA, Curiosity REMS weather feed
  • NASA, Curiosity raw images

Reading

  • Curiosity blog, sols 4689 to 4694
  • Curiosity blog, sols 4723 to 4730
  • Hassler et al. (2014), Science 343, surface radiation at Gale crater
  • Tobler (1993), hiking function, NCGIA Technical Report 93-1

Real in this preview

  • The orbital image, the slope bands and Curiosity's track
  • Both routes, computed on the terrain model by the project's routing script
  • The weather record and the navigation camera photo

Assumed

  • Walking speed, the suit factor of 0.5, the 20 degree slope limit and 30 minutes at the station
  • The start point, a notional rover park

Not built yet

  • Picking your own start and destination
  • Pan and zoom, the thermal layer, photos at every station
  • Public deployment
